newsitem.title: USA: Dodgers says News Corp. interested in team.
newsitem.headline: Dodgers says News Corp. interested in team.

text.p: LOS ANGELES - Rupert Murdoch's News Corp. is in talks to buy the Los Angeles Dodgers, one of America's best known baseball franchises, for more than $350 million, sources said Tuesday.

The Dodgers said Tuesday that team owner Peter O'Malley, who announced in January his intention to sell the storied franchise, has asked Major League Baseball for permission to discuss the sale with Fox Group, a News Corp. affiliate.
The Dodgers, controlled since 1950 by the O'Malley family, said Fox was one of several groups that had expressed interest in the team.
A spokesman for Major League Baseball said its Executive Council will consider the request. A News Corp. spokesman declined to comment.
But a source close to News Corp. confirmed the two sides were in talks, adding, "Something should happen in the middle or end of next week."
The Los Angeles Times and Newsday reported on Monday that Fox was interested in buying the Dodgers, one of the premier franchises in sports.

The Wall Street Journal, quoting people familiar with the situation, reported Tuesday that News Corp. has agreed to pay about $350 million to buy the team, which played in Brooklyn before moving to Los Angeles for the 1958 season.
A spokesman for Major League Baseball said the highest reported price for a major league baseball team was the $173 million paid in 1993 for the Baltimore Orioles.

The Dodgers have won nine National League pennants and five World Series titles since moving from Brooklyn. The team, which has a reputation for developing major league stars, has finished first or second 19 times in the National League West in the past 27 seasons.
Fox already has national broadcast rights for Saturday afternoon baseball games. The network also has rights to weekly broadcasts of National Footbal League games.
